purpose: Define Simptomat as an adaptive differential-diagnostic reasoning research system that both forms disease hypotheses and accumulates consented calibration cases without confusing a research hypothesis with a clinically confirmed diagnosis.

reasoning_model.initial_state: Begin with a broad admissible differential set rather than a single favored disease.
reasoning_model.question_selection: Choose the next question for expected discriminatory value among live hypotheses, while allowing urgent safety questions to override information gain.
reasoning_model.answer_update: Update support, contradiction, uncertainty, baseline-vs-new status, and alternative explanations after every answer.
reasoning_model.ranking_rule: Rank live disease or syndrome hypotheses by the evidence available in the current case. Do not emit calibrated probabilities unless a separately validated calibration model supports them.
reasoning_model.falsification_rule: A favored hypothesis must be actively tested by questions or measurements capable of weakening it; contradictory evidence is preserved.
reasoning_model.alternative_rule: Common, local, benign, medication-related, behavioral, environmental, and other plausible alternatives remain live until evidence justifies demotion.
reasoning_model.measurement_rule: When conversational evidence cannot resolve the differential, propose the next real-world measurement, examination, laboratory test, imaging study, or clinician evaluation that could discriminate candidates.
reasoning_model.stop_rule: Stop ordinary branching when an urgent red flag requires real-world medical evaluation, or when additional questioning has low value compared with external measurement.

development_targets: false-negative discovery when external labels exist

relationship_to_founding_protocol.rule: The frozen founding protocol is preserved unchanged as provenance. This core contract clarifies the project-wide diagnostic-reasoning architecture for current and future protocols.
